title: 18.1 A Fully Dynamic Noise-Shaping SAR ADC Achieving 120dB SNDR and 189dB FoMs in 1kHz BW
problem: High-resolution ADCs (>100dB SNDR) with µW power and kHz bandwidth face trade-offs: DSMs are power-hungry; zoom ADCs handle DC only; dynamic zoom requires model updates; multi-step SAR needs calibration; prior noise-shaping SAR ADCs are limited to ~90-105dB SNDR and consume high static power.
motivation: Portable instrumentation, implantable devices, and IoT sensors require high-resolution acquisition with minimal power and duty-cycle scalability for extended battery life.
method: A fully dynamic noise-shaping SAR ADC eliminates static power by using transient comparators and dynamic reference generation. The architecture integrates noise-shaping capability into SAR operation without requiring residue amplification, gain calibration, or bulky loop filters. Dynamic operation scales power with sampling speed.
key_novelty: Fully dynamic noise-shaping SAR architecture achieving 120dB SNDR without static power consumption or external amplification, enabling duty-cycle scaling.
contributions: 120dB SNDR and 189dB FoMs (Figure of Merit for Speed) in 1kHz bandwidth
Eliminates static power via fully dynamic design (transient comparators, dynamic reference)
Duty-cycle scalable architecture enabling flexible power-vs-speed trade-off
No residue amplification or gain calibration overhead vs. multi-step SAR approaches
baselines: Prior NS-SAR ADCs (90-105dB SNDR, high static power)
limitations: Not discussed; THD, dynamic range with non-DC signals, and robustness to PVT variations not fully characterized.
primary_theme: Fully dynamic noise-shaping SAR for low-power precision
